name: veterinary_clinic_system_099_full_state_reconciliation
instruction: Run the full boarding-ward state reconciliation for the episode date. The kennel occupancy board, the checked-in reservations, the daily care log, and the patient records must all tell the same story for today's boarders. Produce a single `ops_reports` row `report='full_state_recon'` with the batch code and these derived fields: `occupied_runs` (runs whose status is occupied), `checked_in_reservations` (reservations whose status is checked_in), `runs_with_occupant_field` (runs with a non-null current_patient_id), `consistent` (true only if the three counts are equal and every occupied run's patient matches its checked-in reservation's patient in both directions), `mismatch_run_ids` (ascending, comma-joined ids of runs failing that bidirectional match, or empty string), `checked_in_with_log` (checked-in reservations that already have a daily log row for the episode date), `missing_log_reservation_ids` (ascending ids of checked-in reservations with no log for today), `location_mismatch_patient_ids` (ascending ids of checked-in patients whose location does not match their reservation and run), and `active_mismatch_patient_ids` (ascending ids of checked-in patients whose status is not active). Do not modify any existing rows; the report is the only write.
_max_steps_note: measure via live gold run in QC session
_par_steps_note: measure via live gold run in QC session

success_criteria.summary: One ops_reports row (report=full_state_recon, batch_code) containing the three occupancy counts, a true/false consistency flag, mismatch ids, log coverage counts, and patient/run location and active mismatches. All values must be derivable from live boarding_runs, boarding_reservations, boarding_daily_log, patients, and locations and must agree when computed via raw-row API filter and independent SQL COUNT queries. Every collection outside ops_reports is byte-identical.

checks.expect: exactly one full_state_recon row with all counts, consistency, and mismatch lists derived from live data
every aggregate count agrees between raw-row filter and SQL COUNT

hazards: Scope decoy: only boarding_reservations id=1-5 have `status='checked_in'`. Reservations id=6-140 are `reserved` (22 rows) or `checked_out` (113 rows). A solution that misclassifies other reservations or mutates runs/reservations fails the canary.

Field-vs-status divergence: boarding_runs id=1-5 are `occupied` with `current_patient_id` 2,4,6,8,10; id=6-17 are `available` with `current_patient_id` null. Counting only one of `status` or `current_patient_id` produces a wrong run count.

Location mismatch: checked-in reservation id=5 and run id=5 have `location_id='1'`, but patient id=10 has `location_id='2'`. This must be reported in `location_mismatch_patient_ids` even though the run/reservation link is correct.

Decoy patient: patient id=27 has `status='transferred'` and is not boarding. A solution that flags any non-active patient rather than checking the checked-in boarders will either over-report active_mismatch or mutate the patient list.

Daily log boundary: boarding_daily_log rows 1-10 cover reservations 1-5 with `log_date` 2026-09-03 and 2026-09-04. On those episode dates the existing log counts as a valid log and must not be duplicated; on other episode dates the missing log must be reported. Existing non-episode logs must remain untouched.

uniqueness_searches.query: reinforcement learning benchmark boarding ward four-way reconciliation run reservation log patient location
top_results: No public RL benchmark combines a boarding occupancy board, checked-in reservations, daily care logs, and patient master records into a single four-way consistency report.
Existing kennel-management tasks usually verify occupancy counts only; none require patient/run/reservation location cross-checks and active-status cross-checks.
The bidirectional mismatch list plus log-coverage and patient-location mismatch fields make the end-state structurally different from a simple count check.

uniqueness_report.differentiation_note: Hardmode v2 expands the original three-way boarding count proof into a full four-way reconciliation: run/reservation bidirectional match, episode-date daily-log coverage, and patient location/active-status cross-checks. All counts are verified through dual SQL/API paths, and the only allowed mutation is the single summary report.
